sections.h: The startup recruiting stack by stage

Series A and B (50+ hires): add structured assessments (HackerRank for engineering), and Deel once you hire across borders. Keep Noon running on the roles that need outbound sourcing; its flat plan does not grow with seats.

A Series A stack with Ashby (from about $300 a month for small teams), Metaview and a paid Noon plan typically lands in the low thousands per month, well below the cost of one agency placement fee, which commonly runs 20% to 25% of first-year salary.

sections.h: What counts as an AI recruiting tool

A tool that needs a recruiter to drive every search saves minutes; one that completes the task saves headcount-sized time.

description: Seven candidate fraud detection tools ranked for 2026, from application screening and ATS level identity checks to live deepfake detection in interviews and post offer verification: Noon, Greenhouse Real Talent, Talview, GetReal Security, Pindrop, Checkr and Certn.
intro: Verdict first: no single product catches every fake candidate, because fraud shows up at three different moments. A fabricated profile arrives with the application, a proxy or deepfake appears in the interview, and a borrowed identity surfaces at the background check. The best setup puts one tool at each gate. Pindrop says one in six job applicants showed signs of fraud, and GetReal Security's candidate fraud page cites a Gartner forecast that a quarter of applicants will be fake by 2028. We ranked seven tools by how early they stop a fraudulent candidate, how much recruiter time they save and how clearly they explain each flag.

ranked.why: Noon runs fraud checks on every inbound applicant and every sourced profile before a recruiter spends time on them. Applications pulled from your ATS are checked for VPN, proxy and datacenter connections, mismatches between claimed location and observed timezone, and disposable email domains; sourced profiles are built from the public record and tested for overlapping tenures and implausible career jumps. The signals combine into one explainable flag that follows the candidate across roles, and contact emails are verified before any email or SMS outreach goes out. It is free to start, with paid plans quoted per team.

Greenhouse Real Talent adds fraud detection, identity verification and AI candidate matching inside the ATS, so suspicious applications are flagged and spam is blocked where recruiters already work. If Greenhouse is your system of record, this is the lowest friction way to add a first fraud gate.

Talview's candidate verification matches a selfie or ID scan against a base image and keeps checking face, voice and device during the interview, which is the most direct answer to proxy interviewing. It works best when your interviews or assessments already run on Talview.

GetReal Security detects manipulated audio and video in live meetings and has a candidate fraud solution aimed at imposters using deepfakes in remote interviews. Pick it when a fake hire would be a security incident, for example in engineering roles with system access.

Pindrop applies its voice and deepfake detection, a large signal set and a database of known bad actors to calls and virtual meetings, including fake job candidates. It suits enterprises whose security teams already buy this category.

Checkr verifies identity, employment and criminal history at the offer stage through ATS integrations. It will not stop a fake applicant from consuming interview time, but it is the last gate before access is granted.

Certn covers credential and employment verification, international checks in more than 200 countries and territories and continuous monitoring after hire. It is the stronger pick when you hire across borders or need to recheck workers over time.

sections.h: Three gates where fraud gets caught
p: Think of candidate fraud as a pipeline problem. At the application gate, the question is whether the person and the work history are real; network signals, email reputation and career consistency checks answer that cheaply and at scale. At the interview gate, the question is whether the person on camera is the person who applied; face, voice and device verification or deepfake detection handle that. At the offer gate, the question is whether the identity and credentials hold up legally; background screening answers it.

Most teams start at the last gate because they already pay for background checks. That is the most expensive place to discover a problem, after a recruiter screen, a hiring manager interview and a technical loop. Moving detection to the application stage is what saves the most hours. For the screening tools that sit next to these products, see our AI interview tools ranking.

sections.h: How to choose for your stack
p: If you already run Greenhouse, turn on Real Talent and measure how many flags it raises in a month before buying anything else. If your sourcing and first screening happen in one place, a tool that scores fraud at the same moment it evaluates fit, such as Noon's candidate fraud screening, keeps the flag next to the evaluation rather than in a separate dashboard.

Remote engineering and IT hiring justify an interview stage tool. Talview is the pick when you want verification wrapped around the interview, while GetReal Security and Pindrop fit organizations where the CISO owns the risk. Keep Checkr or Certn for the offer stage regardless; they answer legal and compliance questions the other tools do not. Teams comparing broader platforms can start with our AI hiring tools list or the enterprise recruiting software ranking.

sections.h: What a good fraud flag looks like
p: A useful flag names the signals that fired, such as a datacenter IP plus a timezone that does not match the stated city, and lets a recruiter decide. A bare risk score with no explanation trains people to ignore it, and it creates fairness problems if candidates are rejected on signals nobody can describe. Ask every vendor to show a sample flag and the audit trail behind it.

Plan for false positives. Candidates travel, use corporate VPNs and change email providers. Treat one anomaly as context and several together as a reason for a verification step, such as a live video call with ID, rather than an automatic rejection.

faq.q: What is candidate fraud?
faq.a: Candidate fraud covers fabricated resumes, fake or borrowed identities, proxy interviewers who stand in for the real applicant, and deepfake audio or video used in remote interviews. It ranges from embellishment to organized schemes to gain system access.

faq.q: What is the best candidate fraud detection tool?
faq.a: Noon ranks first for catching fraud at the application and sourcing stage, Greenhouse Real Talent is the easiest add for Greenhouse users, and Talview leads for verifying identity during interviews. Most teams combine one early check with a background check at offer.

faq.q: Can background checks catch fake candidates?
faq.a: They catch some identity and credential problems, but only at the offer stage, after the fraudulent candidate has used interview time. Earlier checks on applications and interviews stop fraud sooner.

faq.q: How do you detect a deepfake in a job interview?
faq.a: Interview stage tools such as GetReal Security, Pindrop and Talview analyze audio, video and device signals during the call. Simple steps help too: ask the candidate to turn their head, hold up ID and answer follow up questions about details on their resume.

faq.q: Do fraud detection tools create bias risk?
faq.a: They can if candidates are rejected on unexplained scores. Choose tools that show which signals fired, route flags to a human decision and give candidates a way to verify themselves.

faq.q: Is there a free candidate fraud detection tool?
faq.a: Noon is free to start and includes fraud checks on inbound and sourced candidates. Interview stage deepfake tools and background screening are paid, with Checkr priced per check.

title: Best RocketReach Alternatives for Recruiters
seoTitle: Best RocketReach Alternatives 2026: 6 Ranked for Recruiters | BestRecruitmentTools.com
h1: The best RocketReach alternatives for recruiters in 2026
description: Six RocketReach alternatives ranked for recruiters in 2026: Noon, ContactOut, Lusha, Apollo, Juicebox and SeekOut, compared on candidate search, personal email and phone coverage, outreach and published pricing.
intro: Why do recruiters leave RocketReach? Usually not because the emails are wrong. RocketReach is a phone and email finder, and it does that job; the friction starts when a recruiter wants the tool to also find the right candidates, reach them and keep the pipeline moving. The six tools below solve different parts of that gap. Two are straight contact finders with better personal email coverage or a cheaper free tier, one is a sales platform that recruiters borrow, and three are sourcing tools that search for candidates first and reveal contact details second. Prices and figures come from each vendor's own site, checked on the day we updated this page.

ranked.why: Noon replaces the lookup step and the work around it. Its AI sourcer searches for candidates against your requirements, finds and verifies email addresses, then runs personalized email and SMS sequences and syncs results to your ATS, so a recruiter is not exporting rows from one tool into another. If you are weighing a full switch, read how Noon and RocketReach differ for recruiting teams. It is free to start, with paid plans quoted per team.

ContactOut is the closest like for like swap. Its homepage reports 150 million personal emails and 100 million direct dials, and personal email is what most candidates actually read. The Chrome extension works on profile pages, and a search portal and email campaigns are included. Pick it if RocketReach's work emails were bouncing off candidates who do not check their employer inbox.

Lusha has the friendliest free plan in this group: up to 40 credits a month with a browser extension and CRM integrations. It was built for sales teams, so there is no candidate pipeline, but for a recruiter who needs a handful of phone numbers a week it costs nothing to try. Its certifications list, from SOC 2 Type II to ISO 42001, also helps when legal asks questions.

Apollo bundles a contact database with email sequencing in one sales platform, and its free plan is real. Recruiters borrow it for the combination of lookup and outreach at a low entry price. Expect sales language everywhere, and expect to adapt filters built for buyers to candidate searches. Our Apollo review covers where it fits a recruiting team.

Juicebox flips the order: describe the person you need in a sentence and it returns ranked profiles, then reveals email and phone. Its pricing page lists a free plan with limited searches and a Starter plan at $99 per seat per month that includes unlimited searches and 500 export credits. Choose it if the slow part of your day is finding names, not finding emails.

SeekOut is the enterprise option. It reports more than one billion candidate profiles and offers specialist pools for security cleared talent and healthcare, plus rediscovery of past applicants in your ATS and a Chrome extension. It costs more and takes longer to roll out than a contact finder, which makes sense only for teams hiring at scale or in those specialist markets.

sections.h: Contact finder or sourcing tool: decide before you trial
p: Most RocketReach users fall into one of two camps. The first already knows who to contact, because the names came from a job board, a referral or their own search, and only needs reliable emails and phone numbers. For that camp, ContactOut and Lusha are direct replacements and the trial is simple: run the same 50 candidates through each and count the replies.

The second camp spends more time finding candidates than reaching them. Swapping one contact finder for another will not change much for them. A sourcing tool such as Noon, Juicebox or SeekOut changes the workflow instead, because search, evaluation and contact reveal happen in one place. Our candidate sourcing rankings go deeper on that category.

sections.h: Two more contact finders worth a look
p: Wiza and Hunter did not make the ranked list, but both have clear published pricing. Wiza's free plan includes 20 valid emails and 5 phone numbers, and its email plan is listed at $83 per user per month billed at $990 a year with unlimited email reveals. Hunter's free plan includes 50 monthly credits and its Starter plan is listed at $49 a month. Both are email first and light on recruiting features.

sections.h: How we tested the shortlist
p: We favored tools that recruiters can trial without a sales call, checked each vendor's pricing and data claims on its own site, and ranked by how much of the RocketReach workflow each one improves for hiring rather than selling. Vendor data counts are self reported and not independently audited. Our full scoring method is on the how we rank page, and if your search started with a different data vendor, see the ZoomInfo alternatives and Apollo alternatives lists.

faq.q: What is the best RocketReach alternative for recruiters?
faq.a: Noon ranks first because it finds candidates, verifies their emails and runs email and SMS outreach in one workflow. If you only need a contact finder, ContactOut is the closest direct swap.

faq.q: Is there a free alternative to RocketReach?
faq.a: Yes. Lusha's free plan includes up to 40 credits a month, Apollo has a free plan, Wiza's free plan includes 20 emails and 5 phone numbers, and Hunter's free plan has 50 monthly credits.

faq.q: Which RocketReach alternative has the most personal emails?
faq.a: Among the tools here, ContactOut reports the largest personal email dataset, at 150 million personal emails on its homepage. Coverage claims are self reported, so test with your own candidate list.

faq.q: Should a recruiting team use a sales data tool?
faq.a: It can work for lookups, but sales tools filter by buyer attributes and price for sales seats. Teams that hire every week usually get more from a tool built around candidate search and pipelines.

title: Best Recruiting Chatbots for High-Volume Hiring
seoTitle: Best Recruiting Chatbots 2026: 6 Ranked for Hourly Hiring | BestRecruitmentTools.com
h1: The best recruiting chatbots in 2026
description: Six recruiting chatbots ranked for 2026: Paradox, Humanly, Fountain, Sense, Talkpush and Phenom, compared on screening, scheduling, texting, voice and who each one is built for.
intro: A recruiting chatbot earns its cost in the hours between an application and a recruiter's first look. Hourly applicants apply to several jobs at once and accept the first employer that answers, so a bot that replies in seconds, asks the knockout questions and books an interview slot can decide whether a store opens fully staffed. We ranked six chatbots on what they automate after the first message, how they reach candidates (text, chat, WhatsApp or voice), how they connect to your ATS and which kind of employer each one fits. Every product page was checked on November 10, 2026, and no vendor paid for placement.

ranked.why: Paradox is the benchmark. Its assistant, Olivia, handles conversational apply, scheduling, hiring events and a CRM, and the company lists Chipotle, 7-Eleven, General Motors and Houston Methodist among its clients. It plugs into Workday and SAP SuccessFactors, which matters for large employers that will not replace their system of record. Choose it if you hire thousands of hourly workers a year and can absorb an enterprise rollout.

Humanly ranks second because it covers the steps after the chat as well: its AI Recruiter screens and schedules, an AI Interviewer runs structured first rounds and a notetaker records later interviews. The site claims a 4.8 out of 5 candidate rating and more than 1,000 high volume teams as users. It is a good fit for regional chains and health systems that want Paradox style automation with a lighter footprint.

Fountain is a frontline hiring platform with an applicant tracking system, onboarding and shift scheduling, plus voice agents such as Anna, an AI recruiter that screens candidates around the clock. Buy it when the chatbot is one part of a wider move to a single frontline system rather than an add-on to an existing ATS.

Sense is the pick for staffing agencies. Beyond its chatbot, it offers mass texting, WhatsApp, an AI receptionist for inbound calls and redeployment campaigns that reach contractors as assignments end. Corporate teams can use it too, but the staffing platform is where it stands apart from the others on this list.

Talkpush is an AI-powered ATS and CRM with chat and voice agents coordinated by a lead agent called Clara. The vendor stresses screening in any language and at any volume, and lists BPO and contact center hiring first among its industries. Choose it if you are replacing your ATS and hire across countries.

Phenom is a talent platform first, with an intelligent career site, CRM, automated interview scheduling and agents for voice screening and fraud detection. Its chatbot is strongest as part of that suite. It suits large employers that also want internal mobility and workforce planning, and it is too broad for a team that only needs a screening bot.

sections.h: What a recruiting chatbot actually does
p: The basic job is answering applicant questions and collecting answers to a few knockout questions: age, shift availability, work authorization, a license or a commute radius. The better products then act on those answers. They reject or advance the applicant, book a slot on the hiring manager's calendar, send reminders the day before and update the ATS without a recruiter touching the record.

Text messaging is still the channel that matters most for hourly work, which is why Paradox, Sense and Humanly lead with SMS. Voice is the newer layer. Fountain, Talkpush and Phenom all now sell voice agents that call or answer applicants, which helps with candidates who will not type long answers on a phone. For a deeper look at that format, see our ranking of AI interview tools.

sections.h: Chatbot or full platform: the real buying decision
p: Four of the six vendors also sell an ATS. That changes the project. Adding Paradox or Sense on top of Workday, SAP or a staffing ATS is an integration project measured in weeks or months; moving to Fountain, Humanly's ATS or Talkpush means migrating jobs, applicants and reporting as well. Decide which path you want before booking demos, because every vendor will pitch its widest bundle.

If your bottleneck is response time, a bolt-on is usually enough. If your current system cannot handle mobile apply, texting or hiring events at all, replacing it may be cheaper than patching it. Our high-volume hiring ranking covers the ATS side of that choice.

sections.h: Questions to ask before you sign
p: Ask each vendor to run your own screening flow in the demo, including a candidate who fails a knockout question and one who wants to reschedule. Ask what happens when the bot cannot answer a question and how fast a human picks it up. Ask for the share of conversations that finish without recruiter help at a customer like you, not an average across all clients.

Then check compliance. Bots that score or reject applicants can fall under automated hiring rules such as New York City Local Law 144, and texting consent rules apply to every SMS. Fake applications are also rising, so confirm whether the product checks identity or pairs with a fraud detection tool.

faq.q: What is the best recruiting chatbot?
faq.a: Paradox is the strongest choice for large hourly employers because of its scheduling, hiring events and Workday and SAP integrations. Humanly is the best alternative for teams that also want AI interviews, and Sense is the best fit for staffing agencies.

faq.q: How much do recruiting chatbots cost?
faq.a: None of the six vendors publishes full pricing. Expect quote based annual contracts tied to hiring volume or employee count, with enterprise rollouts priced well above mid-market deals.

faq.q: Do recruiting chatbots replace recruiters?
faq.a: No. They take over repetitive messages, knockout questions and scheduling. Recruiters still handle offers, difficult conversations and hiring manager relationships, and they should review any automated rejection rules.

faq.q: Are chatbots useful for salaried roles?
faq.a: Less so. Professional candidates expect a person to contact them, so chatbots are most useful for hourly, frontline and contact center roles where speed and volume matter more than a personal pitch.

title: Best Restaurant Hiring Software
seoTitle: Best Restaurant Hiring Software 2026: 6 Tools Ranked | BestRecruitmentTools.com
h1: The best restaurant hiring software in 2026
description: Six restaurant hiring software tools ranked for 2026: Workstream, Harri, 7shifts, Homebase, HigherMe and Paradox, compared on price, text to apply, AI screening and fit for single stores or chains.
intro: 15.8 million people will work in US restaurants and foodservice in 2026, about 100,000 more than last year, according to the National Restaurant Association's 2026 State of the Industry report. Every one of those jobs has to be refilled when a server or line cook moves on, so restaurant hiring software is judged on a narrow test: how fast it turns a job post into a confirmed interview. We ranked six products on that test, then on price and on whether they suit one location or hundreds. Each vendor's own site was checked on November 11, 2026, and no vendor paid to be included.

ranked.why: Workstream takes first place because it covers every step of crew hiring that eats a manager's time. Applicants can text to apply, jobs go out to a large network of boards, and AI agents phone or video screen candidates before scheduling them. Packages are quoted, so it fits operators with five or more locations better than a single cafe.

Harri is built only for hospitality, which shows in the details: hiring sits next to scheduling, labor law compliance and HR in one platform. It adds AI screening calls and candidate matching in its higher bundle. Choose it if you run a restaurant group or hotel brand with a corporate HR team and want one vendor for the workforce.

7shifts is the best value for independent restaurants. The free plan covers a single location, and paid plans start at $39.99 per location per month. Hiring is a module inside the scheduling app: post a job, ask screening questions, move applicants through stages and send onboarding paperwork, so a new hire lands on the schedule without retyping.

Homebase gives small restaurants free job posting and applicant tracking, plus an AI hiring assistant that screens applicants and books interviews. Its Basic plan is free for one location with up to ten employees, and paid tiers add payroll and team tools. It is the easiest starting point for an owner who does the hiring personally.

HigherMe suits franchisees who hire crew every week. Candidates apply by text, NextMatch prescreens them, and payroll and onboarding are in the same product. The company says more than 20,000 locations use it and that its customers average two days from application to hire, a claim worth testing with references from your own brand.

Paradox is the choice for national chains with enterprise HR systems. Its assistant, Olivia, texts applicants, answers their questions and books interviews, and it connects to large HR suites. It is more than most restaurant groups need, but at thousands of hires a year the automation pays back.

sections.h: Single store, franchise group or chain
p: The right tool depends mostly on how many locations hire at once. A single restaurant needs a free or cheap job post and a simple list of applicants, which is why 7shifts and Homebase lead for owners. Franchise groups hiring dozens of crew members a week need text to apply and automatic screening, which HigherMe and Workstream are built for. Chains and hotel brands need permissions by region, reporting across units and integration with HR, which is where Harri and Paradox fit.
If you are already paying for a scheduling app, check its hiring module first. Hiring inside the scheduling tool saves a step on every new hire, and both 7shifts and Homebase include it.

sections.h: Features that matter for restaurant hiring
p: Ignore long feature grids and test four things in a demo.
list: Apply by text. Most restaurant applicants use a phone, so a long application form loses many of them.
Screening questions. Ask about availability, food handler cards and the ability to work weekends before an interview is booked.
Self scheduling. Candidates should pick an interview slot without a call from the manager.
Onboarding hand off. Tax forms and handbook acknowledgments should move into payroll and scheduling automatically.

sections.h: When a general ATS is the better buy
p: Restaurant groups that also hire managers, chefs and corporate staff sometimes outgrow hourly tools. If you hire salaried roles regularly, compare these products with our ranking of tools for high volume hiring, the options in small business recruiting and the recruiting chatbots that sit on top of an existing ATS.

faq.q: What is the best restaurant hiring software?
faq.a: Workstream is the strongest all round choice for multi location restaurants. Independent restaurants get the best value from 7shifts or Homebase, and large chains with enterprise HR systems should look at Paradox or Harri.

faq.q: Is there free restaurant hiring software?
faq.a: Yes. Homebase offers free job posting and applicant tracking, and 7shifts has a free plan for a single location. Both charge for advanced scheduling, payroll and team features.

faq.q: How much does restaurant hiring software cost?
faq.a: Small business tools start free and charge roughly $30 to $135 per location per month for paid plans. Workstream, Harri, HigherMe and Paradox quote prices based on locations and features.

h1: The best warehouse hiring software in 2026
description: Six warehouse hiring software tools ranked for 2026: Fountain, Paradox, Workstream, Humanly, Sense and Indeed, compared on shift scheduling, screening, rehire and cost.
intro: Peak season is when warehouse hiring software proves its worth. A distribution center that needs 200 pickers, packers and forklift drivers in three weeks cannot have a recruiter phoning every applicant, so the tool has to screen for shift availability, equipment experience and start date on its own, then book the applicant into an orientation slot. We ranked six tools on November 11, 2026 by how well they handle that flow, from the first click on a job ad to the first shift, and by how they cope with rehiring last season's workers.

ranked.why: Fountain ranks first because its logistics hiring page covers the whole hourly warehouse cycle in one product: sourcing and screening, an AI recruiter that runs voice screens, an applicant tracking system, onboarding and shift scheduling. Its CRM for rehiring former workers is useful for warehouses that bring the same seasonal crew back every year. It is a poor fit for salaried supervisor and engineering hiring.

Paradox suits the largest networks. Its trucking and logistics page describes conversational recruiting through its assistant Olivia, two way text messaging and automated interview scheduling, and names GEODIS Americas and U.S. Xpress as customers. It integrates with Workday, SAP and Indeed. Pricing and rollout are aimed at enterprises, so a single building will find it heavy.

Workstream now sells itself as HR and payroll for hourly businesses, and its dock worker hiring page pairs an applicant tracking system with active sourcing, voice AI screening, a talent network and shift scheduling. That makes it a strong pick for regional operators who want hiring and payroll from one vendor. It started in restaurants, so check references from warehouse customers.

Humanly's transportation page bundles an AI recruiter, AI interviewer, notetaker, CRM and ATS, with conversational screening and automated scheduling. The company claims 55% less application drop off, twice the interview show rate and 20% better first day attendance for customers; treat those as vendor figures and ask for warehouse references. Pricing is quote only.

Sense is the pick for staffing firms that fill warehouse orders for clients. Its manufacturing and warehousing page lists mass SMS and WhatsApp messaging, an AI chatbot and an AI interviewer, which help redeploy associates when an assignment ends. It sits on top of an existing ATS and takes time to configure.

Indeed is where most warehouse applicants start, and posting a job is free, with sponsored jobs that Indeed says get more applications than free posts. It is the right first step for a small warehouse, but it does not screen for shifts or schedule orientation, so volume can bury a single hiring manager.

sections.h: What warehouse hiring software has to do
p: Hourly warehouse hiring fails at the gaps between steps: the applicant who never hears back, the interview that gets no reminder, the new hire who does not show for orientation. Rank any tool on the following points before you look at price.
list: Knockout questions for shift, weekend availability, lifting requirements and forklift certification
Self scheduling for interviews and orientation, with text reminders
Mobile application in a few minutes, in English and Spanish
Rehire pools for last season's workers, with eligibility flags
Onboarding paperwork and I-9 steps that finish before day one
Reporting on show rates by source and by site

sections.h: Direct hire, agency or both
p: Many distribution centers run a mixed model: a core direct workforce plus agency temps for peak. If an agency supplies most of your temps, the agency's own tooling does the screening and your software only needs to cover direct hires. If you are converting temps or reducing agency spend, pick a tool with a rehire CRM so you can approach strong temps directly when their assignment ends.

Supervisors, maintenance technicians and operations managers usually come through a standard applicant tracking system rather than an hourly tool. If those applications already land in Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby or Workable, a screening layer that ranks inbound applicants against each role's non-negotiables can sit beside the hourly stack instead of replacing it.

sections.h: How to run a two week trial
p: Ask the vendor to run one real requisition, such as night shift pickers, at one site. Measure application completion, time from application to scheduled interview, interview show rate and first day attendance against the previous month. If the vendor will not run a pilot on a live role, that tells you how much support you will get after signing.

faq.q: What is warehouse hiring software?
faq.a: It is recruiting software built for hourly warehouse and logistics roles. It screens applicants for shift, location and equipment experience, schedules interviews and orientation automatically, and moves new hires into onboarding.

faq.q: What is the best warehouse hiring software?
faq.a: Fountain is the strongest all round choice for warehouse operators. Paradox suits very large networks, Workstream suits regional operators who also want payroll, and Sense suits staffing firms.

faq.q: Can I hire warehouse workers for free?
faq.a: Yes. Indeed lets you post jobs for free, and you can handle screening by phone. Once you hire more than a few people a week, the time spent chasing applicants usually justifies a paid tool.

faq.q: Does warehouse hiring software replace a staffing agency?
faq.a: It can replace part of the agency's work for direct hires, such as screening and scheduling. Agencies still help during peaks because they carry the payroll, workers' compensation and replacement risk.
